intro: You have spent years collecting pieces of Spanish: the present tense and its stem changes, the preterite and the imperfect, the future and the conditional, the subjunctive in two tenses, tú and usted, the connectors that hold a paragraph together. This unit asks you to put all of it to work at once. In the first chapter, two seniors in Cicero edit each other's essays and rebuild the whole map of tenses and moods as a set of questions you can ask about any verb. In the second, a senior in Humboldt Park builds, delivers and defends a five-minute talk in Spanish about why her family's language matters.

The review chapter is not a list of rules to memorize again. It walks through real sentences from real drafts, shows why one form fits and another does not, and teaches a six-pass routine for catching your own errors before anyone else does. The presentation chapter follows a talk from topic to thesis (Sostengo que…), from three supporting reasons with evidence to transitions and a conclusion, and finally to the questions, where you learn to say Entiendo su punto, pero… and mean it.

By the end you will be able to choose the right verb form from context in a longer passage, edit a page of Spanish with a routine you can repeat, and stand in front of a room with five index cards and a claim you can defend. That is the capstone: not a test of what you remember, but a demonstration of what you can do.
bigQuestion: How do you bring everything you know about Spanish together to write, speak and defend an idea of your own?

timeline.t: Antonio de Nebrija publishes the first grammar of Castilian Spanish, laying out its tenses and moods
Cervantes publishes the first part of Don Quijote, still the most read novel in the language
The Real Academia Española is founded in Madrid to describe and standardize Spanish
Puerto Rico comes under United States rule; Spanish remains the language of its people
Gabriela Mistral of Chile becomes the first Latin American writer to win the Nobel Prize in Literature
The Association of Academies of the Spanish Language is founded, joining the academies of Spain and the Americas
Puerto Rican families settle in Chicago's Humboldt Park, and Mexican families in Pilsen and Little Village grow the city's Spanish
Gabriel García Márquez of Colombia wins the Nobel Prize in Literature
The Instituto Cervantes is created to teach Spanish and share the cultures of the Spanish-speaking world
The United States counts more than forty million people who speak Spanish at home, per the Census Bureau's surveys
Spanish is an official language in twenty countries, and a senior in Chicago stands up to defend a thesis in it

words.d: the present perfect — haber plus a participle: he hablado (I have spoken); reports what has happened up to now
the imperfect — background, habit, age and weather in the past: tenía ocho años (I was eight)
the conditional — infinitive plus ía: trabajaría (I would work); pairs with si tuviera
the subjunctive — the mood after triggers like quiero que, es importante que and dudo que
had (imperfect subjunctive) — from tuvieron; Si tuviera tiempo, iría (If I had time, I would go)
however — a contrast connector that opens a sentence and takes a comma after it
therefore — a conclusion connector; use it only when the earlier ideas cause the new one
agreement — article, noun and adjective share gender and number: las conchas frescas
the thesis — the one-sentence claim a presentation defends: Sostengo que…
the evidence — a story, a number with a source, or an example that supports a reason
in the first place, first — a transition that opens the first supporting reason
I understand your point (formal) — the polite first step before pero when defending a thesis

test.why: The present perfect for yo is he plus the participle, and hacer has the irregular participle hecho.

test.q: Cuando yo ___ (tener) diez años, vivíamos en Pilsen.
test.why: Age in the past is background, so tener takes the imperfect tenía.

test.q: Ayer mi tío ___ (arreglar) el horno en veinte minutos.
test.why: A completed event with a stated length takes the preterite arregló; the accent marks the él form.

test.q: Which form means "we will be able"?
test.why: Poder uses the shortened stem podr- and the future nosotros ending -emos: podremos.
Es mejor que is an impersonal trigger with a new subject, so llegar takes the subjunctive lleguen, with the spelling change g→gu.

test.q: Si ___ (saber) la respuesta, te la diría.
test.why: The si clause of an imagined sentence takes the imperfect subjunctive supiera, from supieron; the conditional belongs in the result.

test.q: Which sentence uses a connector correctly?
choices: Estudié mucho. Sin embargo, aprobé el examen.
Llovió toda la noche. Por lo tanto, el campo está mojado.
Tengo hambre. En cambio, quiero comer.
El pan es fresco. Por lo tanto, la tienda es pequeña.
test.why: Por lo tanto needs cause and result; rain making the field wet is the only real chain. The others promise contrasts or conclusions that are not there.

test.q: Which sentence has an agreement error?
test.why: Entrenadores is masculine plural, so the adjective must be buenos.

test.q: What does "Ayer conocí a la nueva profesora" mean?
choices: Yesterday I already knew the new teacher.
Yesterday I recognized the new teacher.
Yesterday I called the new teacher.
Yesterday I met the new teacher.
test.why: Conocer in the preterite means to meet for the first time, and the personal a marks the teacher as the person met.

test.q: Sostengo que la lengua de mi familia ___ (ser) un tesoro.
test.why: Sostengo que states a claim the speaker stands behind, so the indicative es follows.

test.q: Which phrase would open the last supporting reason of a talk?
test.why: Por último means finally and announces the last reason.

test.q: What is the polite first step when a classmate challenges your thesis?
choices: Acknowledge the point: Entiendo tu punto, pero…
test.why: Defending politely means acknowledging first, then disagreeing with a reason.

test.q: Te recomiendo que ___ (mirar) al público al final de cada oración.
test.why: Te recomiendo que is a recommendation trigger, so mirar takes the present subjunctive mires.

test.q: Which reason is supported by evidence the way this unit teaches?
choices: Según el Instituto Cervantes, el español tiene cientos de millones de hablantes.
Todo el mundo sabe que el español es importante.
Creo que hay como mil millones de hablantes, más o menos.
El español es la lengua más bonita, y punto.
test.why: A rounded figure with a named source is honest evidence; guesses and slogans are not.

test.q: What does "No lo leas. Habla." tell a speaker to do?
choices: Do not read it; speak from notes.
test.why: No leas is the negative tú command of leer, and habla is the affirmative command of hablar: do not read, speak.

write.prompt: Escribe el guion breve de tu presentación final: una tesis, tres argumentos con evidencia y una conclusión con una pregunta para el público. Write one Spanish paragraph with a thesis opener, three reasons introduced by en primer lugar, en segundo lugar and por último, one si sentence with the imperfect subjunctive and the conditional, and a closing question.
tips: Use the transitions and connectors from this unit, and check that each one promises the relationship that really follows.
Write the subject above every verb and check the ending; the -o ending belongs only to yo in the present.
Keep the indicative after sostengo que and creo que, and the subjunctive after no creo que, es importante que and te recomiendo que.
In the si sentence, keep the -ra form in the si clause and the -ía form in the result: Si tuviera…, haría….
Read the paragraph aloud from index cards, not from the page, and time it.
